High humidity near 90% and accumulated rainfall exceeding 150 mm in northern areas further suppress maximum temperatures by limiting insolation and promoting evaporative cooling. Market-implied odds reflect this strong observational consensus from official monitoring. A rapid clearing of clouds or unexpected wind shift could allow brief warming toward 28°C, though model consensus and ongoing heavy rain advisories make such shifts unlikely before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the San Francisco International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=ksfo

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official National Weather Service forecasts for San Francisco on September 4 point to a daily maximum in the upper 60s, driven by persistent onshore marine flow and a moderating coastal layer that limits warming despite mostly sunny conditions. This aligns with early-September normals around 70–72°F while recent model runs show little deviation, keeping 70–71°F the market leader at 61.5% implied probability. Secondary bins at 68–69°F and 72–73°F capture residual uncertainty in afternoon mixing and exact wind strength, with traders weighting the stable pattern over any outlier warming. Updated NWS guidance and real-time observations will refine resolution near the daily peak.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current numerical weather prediction models indicate peak temperatures near 30–31°C in São Paulo on September 4 under mostly sunny skies, light northwest winds, and low humidity, supporting the market's tight split between those two outcomes.** 

These conditions reflect typical early-spring warming on the plateau before a stronger cold front arrives over the weekend, with historical September maxima averaging around 24–25°C. Minor model differences in boundary-layer mixing, urban heat island effects, and exact timing of peak insolation explain the close 43%–34% odds, while lower probabilities for 32°C+ reflect limited warming potential ahead of increasing cloud cover. Official INMET station readings around 14–16h local time will determine resolution.

The close market pricing on 30–32°C reflects uncertainty in the exact timing and coverage of any clearing periods that could allow brief warming toward the upper end of the forecast envelope versus more persistent rain keeping readings nearer 29–30°C. Official guidance lists a 26–32°C range, underscoring model spread on boundary-layer moisture and convective timing as the key variables traders are weighting.

eventMetadata.context_description:

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Amsterdam Airport Schiphol Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eham

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) conditions are the dominant driver suppressing Manila's daytime temperatures on September 5.** Official PAGASA guidance and multiple models project a high of 28–30°C under widespread cloud cover, heavy rainfall, and westerly winds, with 80–100% precipitation probability. These factors reduce solar insolation and evaporative cooling, keeping maxima below the September climatological average of ~31–32°C. Recent satellite imagery and PAGASA advisories confirm the monsoon trough's influence over Luzon with no tropical cyclone inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility to alter steering or intensity. Model consensus and ongoing heavy-rain warnings support the market's concentration on 28–30°C outcomes (cumulative ~85% implied probability), with 29°C as the modal bin reflecting the balance between modest diurnal recovery and persistent moisture. Updated PAGASA and NHC-equivalent briefings tomorrow morning will provide the final observational inputs for resolution.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zuuu

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather prediction consensus from sources including the China Meteorological Administration points to a September 6 peak near 33–34 °C in Chengdu, consistent with market-implied probabilities favoring those bins. Persistent subtropical high pressure over the Sichuan Basin promotes subsidence and clear to partly cloudy skies, enhancing daytime solar heating while the urban heat island and surrounding topography limit nocturnal cooling. Minor model spread in cloud cover and boundary-layer moisture accounts for the tight clustering between 33 °C and 35 °C outcomes. A weak frontal passage or scattered showers later in the window could cap the maximum a degree lower, whereas stronger insolation would push readings toward 36 °C. Updated CMA and ECMWF runs ahead of the date will further constrain the precise value.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zsqd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

High humidity near 85–95% and moderate westerly winds further limit temperature rises by enhancing evaporative cooling and reducing solar insolation.
